Build this branch independently of main using the repository's local ESPHome wrapper and pinned ESPHome 2026.9.1. Based on the generated testing guidance:

1. Confirm normal boot, cover-art display, touch/navigation, and readable text without blank frames or repeated restarts.
2. On the 4-inch P4 and 7-inch, play the same playlist for at least the duration that previously showed a decline. Record Heap Free after downloads settle; also record PSRAM Free and Largest Block to distinguish transient image allocations from lasting loss.
3. Include a player without `entity_picture_local`. Confirm remote covers keep updating across many track changes and after dismissing/reopening the screensaver.
4. Stop playback, wait for the screensaver to close, and allow up to two minutes for memory readings to update. Expect a larger recovery in PSRAM than Heap Free because displayed artwork mainly uses PSRAM; persistent connection/dashboard/cache allocations remain. Confirm that restarting playback loads artwork again, and pausing with the screensaver button keeps the artwork visible.
5. Repeat varied-sized JPEG covers and check image cards where configured. Report remaining memory decline or added decode delay. Smoke-test another P4 and the S3 requester when available.

Fixes #2130 · Replaces #2137 (closed by accident, could not be reopened)

**Cause**

Home Assistant reports a cleared `entity_picture` / `entity_picture_local` as the literal string `"None"`, for example while a Music Assistant player briefly goes `idle` between radio stations. The cover art path in `screen_cover_art.yaml` treated any non-`http` value as a relative path. It built `http://<host>:<port>None`, cached that as the source, and retried it on every refresh:

```
[12:11:05.696] artwork_image: Updating image http://192.168.2.32:80None
[12:11:05.727] HTTP_CLIENT: Error parse url http://192.168.2.32:80None
[12:11:05.772] cover_art: Artwork download failed; trying Home Assistant proxy fallback
```

**Change**

- `screen_cover_art.yaml`: treat `"None"` like `unknown`/`unavailable`, and only join relative paths that start with `/`. This matches the existing guard in `image_card_join_url`, and `camera_refresh_policy::valid_state` already treats `"None"` as invalid.
- `button_grid_image.h`: the same `"None"` check in `image_card_join_url` and in the `entity_picture_local` preference path, so the tile falls back to `entity_picture` instead of treating `"None"` as a valid local picture.
- `artwork_controller.h`: the shared `artwork_entity_picture_present` helper now rejects `"None"`. It feeds the dashboard now-playing artwork subscriptions (`button_grid_grid.h`) and the paired remote-artwork handler (`button_grid_image.h`), so a cleared picture no longer leaves stale artwork-content masks.
- `screen_cover_art.yaml`: the secondary-player content probe uses that helper for its two picture bits, so a cleared `"None"` picture no longer marks the secondary player as having artwork. Title and content-id bits are unchanged.

Relative paths now have to start with `/`. Normal HA/MA values are absolute HTTP(S) URLs or root-relative `/api/...` paths. A bare relative value used to produce a malformed URL; now it is rejected instead.

**Testing**

- Added `assert(!artwork_entity_picture_present("None"))` to `tests/firmware/artwork_controller_test.cpp`; the test compiles and passes.
- `scripts/check_cover_art_contract.py` passes; `git diff --check` clean.
- Built from this branch with ESPHome 2026.9.1 and run on an `esp32-p4-86` with a Music Assistant player. Switched between several radio stations (the same scenario as #2130), with the player passing through `idle` four times in about two minutes. No `http://<host>:80None` requests, no `Error parse url`, no 4-char cached picture, and artwork loaded correctly after every switch (FLO, TuneIn, fanart, PNG logos). pullRequests.body:
Fixes #2129

**Cause**

Every transition into the active screen runs `hide_cover_art_view`, which stops `cover_art_delay_timer`. Closing an image modal starts such an `active -> active` generation, so a pending cover art delay is cancelled. Nothing re-arms it until the next playback-state or presence edge, so the panel stays on the home screen while music keeps playing.

From the log in #2129:

```
[11:56:07.855] cover_art: Waiting 10s before showing cover art
[11:56:07.855] display_mode: Starting generation 89: active -> active   <- modal closed, delay cancelled
... no cover art until the next play action at 12:07:53
```

**Change**

At the end of `display_mode_effect_active` in `common/addon/backlight.yaml`, run `cover_art_start_delay` again when all of these hold:

- cover art screensaver enabled, media playing, a cover art entity configured
- target mode is ACTIVE
- no INTERACTIVE or CRITICAL takeover and no alarm takeover

So the delay re-arms whenever the display settles back on the plain active screen, and cover art still never appears over an open modal. Single 20-line hook, no new globals.

**Testing**

Built from this branch with ESPHome 2026.9.1 and run on an `esp32-p4-86`, cover art delay 10s, Music Assistant player:

- Modal opened and closed within a few seconds: cover art returns 10s after closing.
- Modal open for ~30s, then closed: `Waiting 10s before showing cover art` right after close, `active -> cover_art` 10s later.

```
[17:39:23.565] image_card: Closing image modal for camera.front_door_fluent
[17:39:23.567] display_mode: Starting generation 8: active -> active (takeover=none)
[17:39:23.724] cover_art: Waiting 10s before showing cover art
[17:39:33.725] display_mode: Starting generation 9: active -> cover_art (source=media_playback)
```

Repo checks `check_cover_art_contract.py` and `check_backlight_schedule.py` pass.

## Summary

Fix GSL3680 touchscreen startup on the 10-inch JC8012P4A1 panels. Issue #2166 reports successful I2C writes followed by a zero running marker, after which touch is permanently disabled.

The driver now configures the board firmware's three-contact scan count at register `0x80`, performs the hardware reset before that configuration, and uses four-byte firmware page selectors. It verifies uploaded firmware where controller RAM reads are supported, waits up to 300ms for the complete running marker, and retries initialization once. Controllers that NACK executable RAM reads still have to pass the running-marker check; readback mismatches and other bus errors remain failures. Network diagnostics report whether firmware is verified and running.

Related to #2166. The startup-register diagnosis is supported by Linux's Silead driver and a hardware-confirmed JC8012P4A1 fix in [AgentDeck](https://github.com/puritysb/AgentDeck/blob/master/docs/devlog/entries/2026-07-29-03-ips10-gsl3680-scan-core.md); the fix is now confirmed working on a maintainer's V3 panel.

## Practical impact

- Panels that acknowledge register writes but fail to start now receive the corrected scan configuration and four-byte firmware page selectors.
- A slow or transient startup gets a bounded recovery attempt. Corrupted firmware and persistent failures still disable touch and report the failing stage.
- This shared driver affects the 10-inch V1, V2 and V3 panels. Other display models use different touch drivers.

## Documentation decision

## Summary

Improve first-time WiFi setup and recovery using the provisioning changes from [Espframe PR #257](https://github.com/jtenniswood/espframe/pull/257), adapted to EspControl's components and settings UI.

## Practical impact

- Ethernet-only configurations compile without a WiFi component: the reset component includes the WiFi header only when USE_WIFI is enabled. This addresses the outstanding build review comment.

- Development and adopted device packages now enable the captive portal through shared connectivity configuration. Previously the flashed 7-inch development firmware enabled an AP but omitted the setup DNS server, scan form and credential-save route. Package-expansion regressions cover all nine development and ten factory entry points.
- The hotspot setup page uses EspControl's dark cards, labels, inputs and Save button, with an Available Networks list and manual SSID entry. Styles are embedded in gzip/Brotli firmware assets, so setup works offline. Device/MAC headings and the OTA upload panel are removed from this page.
- Saving credentials shows **WiFi details saved**, followed by instructions to reconnect the phone/computer to home WiFi and continue on the display. The confirmation is served directly without redirects, scripts or external requests.
- Setup DNS explicitly uses IPv4 even when station IPv6 is enabled, and correctly reports omitted authority/EDNS records. OS probes retain ESPHome's standard HTTP 200 portal response. Setup responses use no-cache headers.
- USB Improv provisioning is enabled for setup profiles. The default hotspot is now `EspControl_XXXX`, using the last four hexadecimal characters of the device MAC address (for example, a MAC ending in `F3:6A` gives `EspControl_F36A`). Custom AP names and passwords are preserved. The initial loading screen, WiFi setup screen and language refresh show the actual AP name, followed by instructions to visit `192.168.4.1` in a browser. The new wording is included in all 22 display languages.
- Complete reset erases saved WiFi and the Home Assistant API key, and disables compiled-in WiFi before the network component starts. A dedicated ResetBoot component keeps this action independent of package on_boot merging. New credentials provisioned through the hotspot or USB remain selected after subsequent reboots; Partial reset preserves the active WiFi preference.
- The full-reset confirmation includes the WiFi/API-key warning, backup reminder and a labeled input. The red Complete reset button stays disabled until the user types exactly RESET. Cancel, Escape and invalid input do not send a reset request.

Mixed mapping/list on_boot handlers allowed later screen packages to replace the WiFi reset initializer. The 7-inch hardware test exposed this: stored preferences were erased, but compiled WiFi was restored. Reset startup and default hotspot naming now run in the registered ResetBoot component before WiFi starts. An ESPHome code-generation regression reproduces the package replacement and checks that the reset component remains registered.

The imported component retains ESPHome 2026.9.1's scan filtering, credential storage and provisioning endpoints, with upstream licenses and local changes documented in its README. Deployed S3 configurations retain their smaller setup configuration.

## Documentation decision

- [x] Updated public docs or release-facing notes for user-visible behavior/configuration.
- [ ] No docs needed because this does not change user-visible behavior/configuration.
- [ ] Docs follow-up needed before merge; explain below.

Docs notes:

Installation and troubleshooting describe the saved confirmation, USB provisioning, custom hotspots and reset behavior. Manual installation requires ESPHome 2026.9.1 or newer. The local captive portal README records upstream attribution, regeneration and regression checks.

## Testing

- [x] Automated/local checks passed or were run where practical.
- [x] Device testing is required before merge.
- [ ] Device testing is not required; explain why in Notes for testing.

Automated checks:

- Review fix: the production WiFi reset/AP regression and real ESPHome reset-startup code-generation regression passed. A complete 7-inch JC1060P470 V1 Ethernet-only build with ESPHome 2026.9.1 passed; its generated configuration has USE_ETHERNET, no USE_WIFI, and no generated WiFi header. This was a compile check; Ethernet hardware was not flashed or tested.

- Latest setup wording/hotspot update: all 19 product checks passed, firmware translations are in sync, and firmware Home Assistant binding validation/self-tests passed. The production reset/AP regression passed with the expected `EspControl_F36A` name and custom AP/password preservation.

- `python3 scripts/check_tasks.py run ci --no-cache --jobs 4`: all 49 tasks passed for the preceding captive-portal revision, including 85 host firmware tests, web checks, type checking and generated-file validation.
- `python3 scripts/check_tasks.py run-task wifi-setup`: generated asset checks, real UDP DNS with IPv6 off/on, modeled factory-reset/reprovision/three-reboot/partial-reset/storage-failure checks, custom AP/password preservation, and browser checks at 320/360/640 pixels.
- ESPHome 2026.9.1 configuration validation passed for all ten factory profiles, including the experimental 10-inch V3 profile. Real ESPHome code-generation tests verify registered reset startup survives replacement of on_boot actions. This is not a full compile of every profile.
- The latest 7-inch JC1060P470 V1 development firmware fully compiled with ESPHome 2026.9.1; generated defines confirm USE_CAPTIVE_PORTAL is enabled. The S3 factory profile compiled for the preceding reset-startup change. Hosted firmware checks are running.
- `npm run docs:build`: passed, including internal links and anchors.
- Focused reset browser tests passed: typed confirmation, invalid/lowercase/space-padded text, editing/reopening the dialog, Cancel/Escape, a narrow 320px viewport, and a single factory-reset request. Hosted checks are running for the updated head.

Affected display/device, if applicable:

The preceding captive-portal enablement (55e9b55fc) was uploaded successfully over OTA to the 7-inch V1 at 192.168.6.102 on 2026-10-09. ESPHome reported OTA success, and the display responded to both post-reboot ping checks. The user confirmed on 2026-10-09 that Complete reset followed by WiFi setup and reconnection worked on the 7-inch V1 before the latest wording/name update. The latest wording/name revision (d1ef2a759) fully compiled and was flashed over OTA to the same 7-inch V1; ESPHome reported success and both post-reboot ping checks passed. The user also confirmed on 2026-10-09 that the updated setup message and EspControl_XXXX hotspot naming work on the 7-inch V1. Repeated-reboot, Partial reset and other-device physical testing have not been separately confirmed.

Confirm automatic sign-in opens the styled Available Networks form; also check `http://192.168.4.1` directly.
3. Select a network or enter it manually, enter the password and save. Confirm the saved page tells you to reconnect to home WiFi, then complete setup on the display.
4. Confirm Complete reset stays disabled until exactly RESET is typed; test Cancel and Escape. With firmware containing compiled WiFi for network A, perform Complete reset and provision network B. The three-reboot, Partial reset and individual dialog-interaction checks have not been separately confirmed; the host regression uses modeled NVS/WiFi.

## Summary

Media cards can now reorder and hide popup tabs under **Modal Settings**, using the same drag handles, arrows, and switches as the fan editor. **All Controls** and **Cover Art** share these settings and an optional separate power device. - Reorder **Controls**, **Track Position**, **Volume**, **Speakers**, and **Power**, or switch off tabs you do not want. The popup opens the first available tab in the saved order. Unsupported tabs stay hidden, with Controls as a fallback while the main player is available. A single visible tab hides the tab bar.
- **Optional Power** sits inside **Modal Settings**, below the tab list, without explanatory info text. Power starts off and unavailable until a Power Entity is entered. Adding an entity enables Power, including with a custom tab order; it can still be hidden manually. Clearing the entity disables the tab and blocks power actions. Use a Sonos soundbar for playback/volume and a TV, switch, input boolean, light, or fan for power.
- Switching between All Controls and Cover Art retains the power entity, tab order, and visibility choices. Other media types omit these modal options. The default order of the other controls stays the same. The main player's native power capability does not enable Power without an explicitly configured Power Entity.
- Cover Art continues to use its existing external-source playback routing; the separate power target stays fixed. Enough shared state slots are reserved for cards with distinct main, secondary artwork, and power entities.
- If the main player becomes unavailable, the popup can still open its enabled Power tab while the separate device has a known, available state. Playback tabs return when the player recovers; losing both devices closes the popup.

The clock and date drift together to reduce burn-in and share the configured clock text color. The toggle is restored after reboot and included in backups; older backups default it to off. Older firmware hides the unsupported control. Language and color changes refresh the date immediately.
